incident.title: Order Service database connections rejected by active access policy
incident.alert_or_symptom: New Order Management Service database connections are being rejected, causing widespread order-creation and order-update failures while requests using existing database sessions continue to succeed.

technical_evidence.observation: Of 21,800 order-creation and order-update requests between 16:05 and 16:25, 62.4 percent failed and 37.6 percent completed successfully.
Failed requests record SQLSTATE 28000 with the message CONNECT privilege denied for the Order Service database role when a new session is opened to the transactional database.
The Order Service role is recognised and authentication succeeds, but the active database access policy does not grant that role CONNECT access to the transactional order database.
All database replicas are available, replication is healthy and read and write transactions from Authentication, Payment and Inventory services remain within normal operating thresholds.
Requests assigned to existing database sessions continue to complete. Requests requiring a newly opened session fail during database access-policy evaluation before any order query is executed.
A revised database access-policy set was activated at 15:52. The active policy set does not contain the expected CONNECT grant for the Order Service role.

Customers across the United Kingdom and Ireland report intermittent order-submission failures. Some orders succeed, but repeated submission is discouraged because the status of a failed attempt may not be immediately clear.

The evidence directly establishes a database-level access-configuration failure affecting new Order Service connections. It does not indicate database unavailability, an Order Service application exception or failure of another dependency.

service_impact.user_impact_description: Customers across the United Kingdom and Ireland are experiencing widespread order-creation and update failures, although requests using existing database sessions continue to succeed.
service_impact.business_function_affected: Customer order creation and order-status processing
service_impact.workaround_description: A limited number of priority orders can be placed through the approved contact-centre procedure, but customers should not repeatedly resubmit failed online orders until transaction status is confirmed.

environmental_context: The Order Management Service and Transaction Database Cluster are Tier 1 business-critical components.
The Transaction Database Cluster stores order, payment, inventory and customer records.
Authentication, Payment and Inventory services continue to use the database successfully.
Existing Order Service database sessions remain usable, while newly opened sessions are rejected.

recent_changes.description: A revised database access-policy set was activated at 15:52 and does not include the expected CONNECT grant for the Order Service role.

reported_unknowns: Why the expected Order Service CONNECT grant is absent from the active database access-policy set.
The precise number of Order Service instances and connection pools that will require new database sessions before the incident is resolved.
Whether any failed order attempts created partial records or could result in duplicate processing if customers retry.
The expected time for an approved correction and full service recovery.
additional_context: No database outage, data corruption, duplicate order, credential exposure or serious security incident has been confirmed.
The database role name and access-policy findings are provided as controlled diagnostic evidence and no secret value is included.

routing.rationale: The Data Platform Team is primarily responsible for the transaction database and its access policies.
